newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India ends down on industrial data.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India ends down on industrial data.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) closed marginally lower on Thursday amid disappointing industrial production data and first half results.
"The market has been drifting lower, tracking Bombay. In the last couple of weeks, the sentiment has turned much softer," one broker said.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 1.43 points, or 2.31 percent, at 60.46 points, with the premium over the local market at 15.75 percent compared with yesterday's 17.66 percent percent.

The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index closed 19.2 points lower at 3043.30 points after data released on Wednesday showed April-September industrial growth had slowed to 4.8 percent from 12.8 percent last year.

A broker said the GDR market was unnerved by rumours that Telco's November sales figure would be lower than expected, which triggered selling in automobile sector shares. Telco closed 93 cents down, while Bajaj fell 88 cents.
"There is an increasing perception that the Bombay share index's psychological 3,000-level may be broken on the back of poor first half results, certainly by the year-end," the broker said.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 0.37 points, or 0.54 percent, at 67.91, a premium of 29.70 percent over the local market, compared with yesterday's 30.72 percent.
The Korea Composite Index closed provisionally at 744.14, down 2.91 points.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.55 points, or 0.61 percent, at 91.05 , a premium of 3.91 percent after 4.28 percent yesterday.
The Taiwan Weighted Index fell 36.87 points or 0.55 percent to 6,692.49.
